project_specification.project_name: nullius — research book v2: beta-neutral legs and the USD-M perpetual instrument (funding carry, perp fees)
project_specification.addition_summary: Five pre-registered M2 tests failed. COST-1 made the book net of turnover. The in-sample IC→book diagnostic (appendix of docs/preregistration/2026-10-13-m2-composite.RESULT.md) found two things holding the book back: - The research book is dollar-neutral but not beta-neutral. Low-vol's book carries a −0.38 BTC beta, and neutralising it lifts its IR t from 0.69 to 1.11. - The book is a spot book with no funding. The live venue (router, BingX VST) trades USDT-M perpetual swaps, so research scores a different instrument from the one the bot trades. PRD §2.3 names the perp instrument, with funding as carry, as the next lever. This spec adds two evaluation-config options, both defaulting to today's behaviour: - book.beta_neutral - instrument: "perp" (perp closes from the futbars stream, funding accrual charged per symbol, and a binance_usdm fee schedule) It also shows the authoring agent what book and instrument it is scored on.

existing_context.test_baseline: main at fdc7662: gate 1666 passed; evaluator 577; orchestrator 628 passed 5 skipped; signal-agent 846.
existing_context.conventions: Follow CLAUDE.md. A code map from 2026-10-14: - evaluator/_metrics.py compute_node_metrics(returns, scores, *, cost_per_unit_traded=0.0): - weights w = z/Σ|z| (~:620-640), per-date book return, turnover charge (COST-1) - NodeMetrics' fields are fixed - orchestrator/_context.py load_evaluation_context: - parses the evaluation config, refusing unknown keys (_refuse_unknown_keys ~:640) and adding keys with their own validators (see _max_history_days, _evaluation_mode) - context.closes is a lazy {symbol: {date: close}} over the bars stream (_read_close ~:1447) - context.cost_schedule comes from NULLIUS_COST_MODEL_PATH (cost_model.config COST_MODEL_PATH_ENV) - Everything downstream reads context.closes: - snapshot_forward_returns / grid_forward_returns (_targets.py) - align_targets - closeout's _oos_target_endpoint, through evaluate_on_dates - _financial_eval - orchestrator/_evaluate.py: - _cost_schedule_from_context (~:746) quotes a uniform taker fee per (date, symbol). It cancels in a centered book (COST-1). A non-uniform per-symbol charge does not cancel: Σ w(r − c) charges a long w > 0 by c and pays a short by c, which is exactly perp funding (longs pay positive funding). - evaluate_node ~:1397 and evaluate_on_dates ~:1644 call compute_node_metrics. - The futbars stream: staging/futbars/symbol=S/date=D with fut_close (rescaled to the spot price scale for 1000-contracts), keyed by the spot symbol S. The funding stream: rows per day D with funding_rate_sum over settlements in (D 00:00, D+1 00:00] (ingest/derivs_backfill.py). A symbol with no perpetual has no rows. - signal-agent _authoring_prompt.py _cost_awareness_part (~:345) reads the evaluation context duck-typed. - packages/cost-model/src/cost_model/binance_usdm.yaml (committed with this spec) is the USD-M fee schedule: venue binance_usdm, taker 5 bps. - The router's live venue: /openApi/swap/v2 perpetuals; the contracts.json fixture has takerFeeRate 0.0005 and makerFeeRate 0.0002.

category.name: Book Construction
category.feature: System scores a beta-neutral dollar-neutral book when per-symbol betas are supplied, so that compute_node_metrics returns a book whose long and short legs carry equal benchmark beta. - compute_node_metrics gains a keyword-only argument, betas, of type Mapping[date, Mapping[str, float]] | None, defaulting to None. None reproduces today's figures exactly. - With betas, each date's z-weights are split into a long leg (w > 0) and a short leg (w < 0). β_L is the weight-averaged beta of the long leg and β_S that of the short leg, over the symbols with a beta. The legs are rescaled to gross gl and 1 − gl, with gl = β_S/(β_L + β_S), so gl·β_L = (1 − gl)·β_S and gross exposure stays 1. Symbols without a beta that date keep their weight unscaled. If β_L + β_S ≤ 0, or a leg is empty, the date falls back to the plain weights, and NodeMetrics' existing fields do not change shape. - The rescaled weights feed the book return, the turnover and the COST-1 turnover charge, so cost reflects what the book trades. The IC is unchanged, because it is rank-based on scores. - test_metrics_beta_neutral.py covers: - a hand-computed two-date example - the book beta (Σ w·β) is 0 within 1e-12 when every symbol has a beta - None equals today's figures - the fallback on degenerate legs - non-finite betas are refused with EvaluatorMetricsError It passes under pytest-xdist. The evaluator member suite passes.

System applies the configured beta-neutral book in every evaluation, so that a campaign with `"book": {"beta_neutral": true}` in its evaluation config returns node and close-out figures from the beta-neutral book. - The evaluation config gains an optional book object: {"beta_neutral": bool, "beta_window_days": int (default 60), "beta_benchmark": str (default "BTCUSDT")}. Unknown keys inside it are refused. When it is absent, book.beta_neutral is false and behaviour is unchanged. The EvaluationContext carries it. - When beta_neutral is on, the context provides point-in-time betas for each evaluation date D. Each is the OLS slope of a symbol's daily close-to-close returns on the benchmark's, over the beta_window_days daily returns ending at D. They are read from context.closes, so the instrument in force is used. No row after D is read. A symbol needs at least 80% of the window's returns, otherwise it has no beta for D. If the benchmark is absent, there are no betas for D. - evaluate_node and evaluate_on_dates pass betas to compute_node_metrics, for both the net figures and the gross diagnostic. Close-out oos_ir follows through evaluate_on_dates; closeout.py is not edited. - test_book_beta_neutral.py, over a tmp sealed snapshot, covers: - a config with beta_neutral gives a node whose book beta is 0 - the betas are point-in-time (a planted future shock does not change the beta at D) - the absent block is unchanged - an unknown key inside book is refused It passes under pytest-xdist. The orchestrator member suite passes (run at -n 2).

category.name: Perpetual Instrument
category.feature: System evaluates signals as a book of USD-M perpetuals when the evaluation config says `"instrument": "perp"`, so that node and close-out figures return perp price returns net of funding carry and perp fees. - The evaluation config gains an optional key, instrument, with values "spot" (the default, unchanged behaviour) or "perp". Any other value is refused. - With "perp": - context.closes is served from the futbars stream's fut_close, keyed by the spot symbol, with the same lazy, point-in-time and validation rules as the bars closes. The bars closes are not read for returns. - Forward returns, alignment, betas and close-out all follow, because they read context.closes. - Scoring universe: on each date, a scored symbol with no perp close at D is dropped from the score vector before alignment. Dropped symbols are counted in the evaluation's fail_detail-free diagnostics, and never zero-filled. This replaces _align's refusal for that case only. - Funding carry: _cost_schedule_from_context adds, for each (D, symbol), the sum of funding_rate_sum over the horizon's holding days, D+1 to D+h. Under the ingest day rule, the settlement at D+1 00:00 belongs to row D, so the window that starts after the D-close entry begins at row D+1. A missing funding row in the window counts 0 and is counted. With Σ w(r − c), longs pay positive funding and shorts receive it. The uniform taker fee stays as well, so COST-1's turnover charge remains the binding fee cost. - The deployment selects perp fees by pointing NULLIUS_COST_MODEL_PATH at packages/cost-model/src/cost_model/binance_usdm.yaml (venue binance_usdm, taker 5 bps, maker 2 bps; committed with this spec, with its tests). If "perp" is configured with a schedule whose venue does not end in _usdm, the context refuses it, naming both. - test_perp_instrument.py, over a tmp sealed snapshot with bars, futbars and funding, covers: - perp returns come from fut_close - funding is charged with the right sign and window (a long in a positive-funding coin earns less than its price return, and a short earns more) - a no-perp symbol is dropped, not refused - the spot default is unchanged - a mismatched venue is refused It passes under pytest-xdist. The orchestrator member suite passes (run at -n 2).

category.name: Agent Contract
category.feature: System tells the authoring agent which book and instrument it is scored on, so that the rendered prompt displays beta-neutral legs, perp funding carry and the per-unit-traded fee when they are configured. - The cost_awareness section renders three new facts, read duck-typed from the evaluation context (an absent attribute means the spot and plain-book defaults): - instrument: spot, or "USD-M perpetual; longs pay and shorts receive funding over the holding period" - book: "dollar-neutral", or "dollar- and BTC-beta-neutral (legs rescaled to equal 60-day beta)" - the fee per unit of traded notional, multiplied by Σ|Δw| It adds one information-only line: for a perp book, persistent funding differences are part of the return, and a beta-neutral book removes market direction, so the signal must earn from cross-sectional differences alone. - Every other rendered section is byte-identical (a test compares them). - test_prompt_book_instrument.py covers: - the perp plus beta-neutral rendering - the default rendering - the byte-identical other sections It passes under pytest-xdist. The signal-agent member suite passes.
